Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: No digital authentication function exists. The biometric CNI is a physical card; there is no digital authentication infrastructure (no online verification portal, no API, no token-based authentication). The World Bank ID4D diagnostic confirmed no online authentication mechanisms exist. The 2023 CIPESA country report found no digital authentication capability described.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: No government portal authentication using digital ID exists. There are no functioning e-government portals requiring digital identity authentication in CAR. Internet penetration was only 14% in 2023, and digital government services are nascent. The national ID is not used for any online government service authentication.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: No mechanism exists for individuals to access their own identity data. Although the 2024 Data Protection Law (No. 24.001) includes a right of access for data subjects, the supervisory authority that would enable enforcement has not yet been established, and no practical mechanism for individuals to view or obtain their identity data has been implemented.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight exists but is not ID-specific. In 2020, the Administrative Court suspended and repealed the government decree raising CNI prices (from CFA 4,500 to higher amounts), finding it violated the Finance Law. This demonstrates general judicial oversight capability over government identity-related decisions. However, there are no dedicated judicial mechanisms specifically for digital ID systems.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration only. A birth certificate is required to obtain a national identity card, establishing a formal link. However, the civil registration system is largely paper-based and severely damaged (60–80% of records destroyed in the 2013 crisis). There is no digital CRVS system, and the ID and civil registration databases are not electronically integrated. The OIF launched a project in 2025 to issue 3,000 birth certificates to unregistered individuals.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: No formal data sharing framework is in place for identity data. The 2024 Data Protection Law (No. 24.001) includes provisions on data transfers (including to CEMAC/ECCAS member states and non-member states), but the supervisory authority tasked with authorizing such transfers has not been established. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic noted no formal interoperability agreements between identity systems.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: No digital ID-specific regulation exists. The existing legal framework for identity dates to the 1960s and does not address digital identity. The 2024 Data Protection Law (No. 24.001) covers personal data broadly but is not specific to digital ID. The CIPESA/Greater Internet Freedom 2023 report and Paradigm Initiative 2024 policy brief both confirmed the absence of a dedicated digital ID law.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: No independent data protection authority has been established. Although Law No. 24.001 (January 2024) mandated creation of a supervisory authority within 12 months, as of 2025 no such authority has been operationalized. The Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts, and Telecommunications serves as an interim oversight body pending the authority's establishment.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national identity card (CNI) serves as legal proof of identity in the Central African Republic. It is required by law enforcement during checks, needed to access banking, receive pensions, and participate in civic life. Citizens without a CNI use voter cards or other documents as alternatives. The card is accepted as a breeder document for other services.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A legal framework for national identity exists, though it is outdated. Key laws include Law No. 60-164 (1960, amended 1962/1964) on national identity cards; Ordinance No. 69-033/69-034 (1969) on civil registration; Family Code (Law No. 97-013, 1998); and the CAR Constitution (2016) guaranteeing the right to identity. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic (2021) noted laws are not adapted to current context. A new Data Protection Law (No. 24.001) was enacted in January 2024.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: Foreign vendors dominate. The national identity card is produced and maintained entirely by Al-Madina, a Lebanese-managed company (contracted 2019). Prior to that, Centrafrique Carte System (CCS, a subsidiary of Ivoire Cartes Systèmes) held the contract (2016–2017). Passports are produced by AFRICARD (Inkript/RGH, Lebanon). The Ministry of Interior's Public Procurement DG objected to the Al-Madina contract for non-compliance with procurement laws; the contract was awarded regardless.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: ID system sustainability is primarily reliant on external arrangements. The biometric CNI is produced under a public-private partnership (PPP) with Al-Madina, a foreign company. External donors (World Bank, UN agencies, African Development Bank) have supported identity-related projects and civil registration. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic was conducted at the request of the government with donor support. Domestic revenue generation from ID fees has been inconsistent and poorly tracked.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The new biometric CNI collects fingerprints and a facial photograph. No iris scan collection has been documented. The provisional récépissé (issued 2014–2019) did not collect biometrics. Biometric voter registration also collects fingerprints (GenKey system used in 2024 voter registration exercise).

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: A mixed system exists. Civil registration records are primarily paper-based (with 60–80% destroyed in the 2013 crisis, no comprehensive digitization). The Al-Madina biometric CNI system uses a digital production database. The ANE voter database (~2 million records) is fully electronic. The national civil registration system remains paper-based and has not been digitized.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: The Central African Republic has a partially deployed national ID system. A biometric national identity card (CNI) with fingerprints and photo is being produced by Al-Madina (a foreign company contracted in 2019). Decentralized issuance campaigns have been conducted in multiple provinces (Bouar, Berbérati, Bossangoa, Mbaïki, Sibut, Birao) through 2023–2025. However, coverage remains very limited and the system is not deployed nationwide. Prior to 2019, only provisional receipts (récépissé) without fingerprints were issued following the 2013 crisis.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: No formal system interoperability exists. The national ID, voter database (ANE with ~2 million records), and civil registration systems are not interconnected. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic (2021) explicitly noted no formal agreements or online protocols between identity systems. The ANE voter database is not linked to the national ID system.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The national ID is accepted (not mandatory) for banking and financial services. Banks require KYC documentation for account opening, and the CNI is accepted. Citizens have reported needing the CNI to collect pensions from banks. However, digital/mobile banking is very limited. The BEAC oversees the banking sector. Mobile money (Orange Centrafrique) is the main financial service for most citizens.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The national identity card carries a fee. The official cost is set by the Finance Law at CFA 4,500 (~USD 7.50). There have been reports of illegal surcharges (CFA 6,000–15,000), which were ruled unlawful by the Administrative Court and addressed in 2025. Some parliamentary constituencies have offered subsidized or free CNI issuance campaigns. The credential is not free as a standard policy.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Some regional cross-border recognition exists within CEMAC. CEMAC standards provide for mutual recognition of passports, driving licenses, and vehicle documents among the 6 member states (Cameroon, CAR, Chad, Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon). CAR is also an ECCAS member, though free movement of persons under ECCAS remains largely unimplemented. The national ID card does not have confirmed formal cross-border recognition. CAR has a relatively favourable visa policy (scored 0.619 on ECCAS integration index, second-highest).

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Enrollment eligibility starts at age 12 (or later than 17 on the scale). Under Law No. 60-164 (1960) and its amendments, Central African citizens aged 12 and above are required to hold a national identity card. A birth certificate or jugement supplétif is required as a breeder document. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic confirmed the mandatory age of 12+.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Enrollment is legally mandatory for all Central African citizens aged 12 and above. Police and security forces conduct document checks (rafles) requiring citizens to present their CNI. Citizens without a CNI have been detained. The Finance Law sets the official price, implying a formal legal obligation. However, enforcement is uneven given the low coverage rates and ongoing security challenges.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Non-nationals are not eligible for the national identity card. The CNI is restricted to Central African citizens. Non-nationals (including refugees and IDPs) do not qualify for the national ID. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic noted that refugees may participate in voter registration with a refugee card or witness, but there is no provision for non-nationals in the national identity system.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Population coverage is below 20%. Pre-2013 coverage was already estimated at less than 20% for national ID cards. The 2013 crisis destroyed 60–80% of existing records and the card production facility. Since 2019, decentralized issuance campaigns have been conducted by Al-Madina but coverage remains very limited. The Paradigm Initiative 2024 brief noted that ANE has the largest digital identity database with close to 2 million records (voter registration), but national ID coverage is substantially lower than 20% of the population (~6.4 million).

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: No evidence of independent security reviews of the national identity system has been found. The Al-Madina contract was awarded without transparent public procurement, and the DG of Public Procurement objected to the process. No third-party technical audits or security assessments of the identity system infrastructure have been documented in available sources.
